Section 0: Master Cartesian Sign Convention & Consistency Rules MANDATORY EXAM FOUNDATION

Every equation, derivation, graph, and numerical value in this document strictly adheres to the standard New Cartesian Sign Convention mandated by NCERT and tested by JEE Main.

1. Origin of Coordinates (The Zero Point)

All axial distances along the principal axis are measured strictly from the **Pole (P) for spherical mirrors and single refracting surfaces, or from the Optical Center (O)** for thin lenses.

2. Incident Ray Axis (The +x Direction)

The direction of propagation of incident light rays is defined as **Positive (+x). Distances measured against the direction of incident light rays are Negative (−x)**.

3. Transverse Heights (±y)

Heights measured perpendicular to and above the principal axis are **Positive (+y) (erect). Heights measured perpendicular to and below the axis are Negative (−y)** (inverted).

4. Real vs. Virtual Definitions

Real Object: Diverging incident rays originate from an actual point ⟹u<0.<br/>Virtual Object: Incident rays converge toward a point behind the interface ⟹u>0.<br/>Real Image: Actual physical intersection of rays. Mirror: v<0 (front). Lens: v>0 (rear).<br/>Virtual Image: Apparent intersection of diverged rays. Mirror: v>0 (rear). Lens: v<0 (front).

The 4 Universal Sign Tables for Real Objects (u<0)

Optical Device Focal Length f Object Pos. u Image Pos. v Magnification m Image Character
Concave Mirror f<0 ∣u∣>∣f∣ v<0 m<0 Real, Inverted (Diminished if ∣u∣>2∣f∣, Magnified if ∣f∣<∣u∣<2∣f∣)
Concave Mirror f<0 ∣u∣<∣f∣ v>0 m>+1 Virtual, Erect, Magnified (Behind mirror)
Convex Mirror f>0 Any u<0 0<v<f 0<m<+1 STRICTLY Virtual, Erect, Diminished for ANY real object!
Convex Lens f>0 ∣u∣>f v>0 m<0 Real, Inverted (Opposite side; v=+2f when u=−2f)
Convex Lens f>0 ∣u∣<f v<0 m>+1 Virtual, Erect, Magnified (Same side as object)
Concave Lens f<0 Any u<0 −∣f∣<v<0 0<m<+1 STRICTLY Virtual, Erect, Diminished for ANY real object!

Section 1: The 12 Master Formula Modules 100% Comprehensive

Module 1: Thin Lens Master Formula & Magnification Network

Extreme Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026

The fundamental Gaussian relation connecting object distance u, image distance v, and focal length f for any thin lens under Cartesian sign convention.

When to Use It: Use whenever a single thin lens forms real or virtual images of an object, or when relating object/image displacements, velocities, or magnification ratios.
MASTER FORMULA
f1​=v1​−u1​
Exam Strategy: Always sketch the lens axis and write Cartesian coordinates immediately before substituting numbers: u<0, real v>0.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • u: Object distance (measured from optical center, u<0 for real object)
  • v: Image distance (v>0 for real image, v<0 for virtual image)
  • f: Focal length (f>0 for convex/converging, f<0 for concave/diverging in air)
  • m: Transverse magnification: m=uv​=ho​hi​​

One-Step Derived Forms

Magnification directly in terms of u and f
m=ff+um = \frac{f}{f + u}m=f+uf​

Derived by multiplying Gaussian equation by u: fu​=vu​−1⟹m1​=1+fu​=ff+u​. Eliminates image distance v in one step.

Magnification directly in terms of v and f
m=f−vfm = \frac{f - v}{f}m=ff−v​

Derived by multiplying Gaussian equation by v: fv​=1−uv​=1−m⟹m=1−fv​. Eliminates object distance u in one step.

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Object placed at two distances gives images of identical size” ⟹ Use f=2u1​+u2​​ immediately.
  • ▸ “Screen and object separated by distance D; lens displaced by d” ⟹ Displacement method: f=4DD2−d2​.
  • ▸ “Real image is 3 times magnified” ⟹m=−3 (real means inverted for thin lens).

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Two Positions for Equal Size Images (NTA Classic) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2026 Jan 28 Shift 1 (u1​=8 cm,u2​=24 cm⟹f=16 cm)
f=2u1​+u2​​

Condition: When an object placed at distances u1​ and u2​ from a convex lens produces images of the exact same size ∣m1​∣=∣m2​∣.

Physics Rule: One image is real (inverted, m=−k) and one is virtual (erect, m=+k). Thus f=2u1​+u2​​.

Displacement Method (Bessel's Method) Verified PYQ
f=4DD2−d2​,O=I1​I2​​,m1​m2​=1

Condition: Screen and object fixed at separation D>4f; lens shifted by distance d between two distinct sharp image positions.

Physics Rule: If D=4f, then d=0 (single position where u=2f,v=2f). If D<4f, no real image can be formed on the screen.

Longitudinal Magnification for Small Object (du) High-Value Variation
mL​=dudv​=m2=(uv​)2=(f+uf​)2

Condition: Small object of axial length du placed along the principal axis.

Physics Rule: Always positive! Real image is elongated along the axis if ∣m∣>1. For a finite rod: mL​=u2​−u1​v2​−v1​​.

1/v vs 1/u Graph Slope & Intercepts Verified PYQ
v1​=u1​+f1​⟹Straight line with Slope =+1

Condition: y=v1​ and x=u1​. y-intercept =+f1​, x-intercept =−f1​.

Physics Rule: Angle made with the x-axis is exactly 45∘ (slope tanθ=+1) for any thin lens.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Object at infinity (u→−∞):
v1​−0=f1​⟹v=f
Rays converge to second focal point F2​.
Object at focus (u=−f):
v1​−(−f1​)=f1​⟹v1​=0⟹v→∞
Rays emerge parallel to principal axis.
Symmetric position (u=−2f):
v=+2f,m=−2f+2f​=−1
Real, inverted image of exact same size; separation D=4f (minimum separation for real image).

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Confusing lens formula with mirror formula: lens is v1​−u1​=f1​, whereas mirror is v1​+u1​=f1​.
  • ⚠ Magnification sign trap: in lens m=+uv​; in mirror m=−uv​.
  • ⚠ Remember: Real image formed by a convex lens is on the other side, so v>0, making m=uv​<0 (inverted).

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A luminous object and a screen are placed a fixed distance D=90 cm apart. A convex lens placed between them produces a sharp image on the screen at two positions separated by d=30 cm. Find the focal length of the lens and the ratio of image sizes.

Given Data: D=90 cm,d=30 cm

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Apply Bessel displacement formula: f=4DD2−d2​.
  2. Substitute values: f=4×90902−302​=3608100−900​=3607200​=20 cm.
  3. Image sizes satisfy m1​m2​=1 with m1​=D−dD+d​=90−3090+30​=60120​=2 and m2​=21​.
  4. Ratio of image sizes is I2​I1​​=m2​m1​​=4.
Final Answer: f=20 cm,I2​I1​​=4

Module 2: Lens Maker's Formula & Medium Immersion Variations

Extreme Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026

Governs how the radii of curvature R1​,R2​, the refractive index of the lens μL​, and the surrounding medium μm​ determine focal length.

When to Use It: Use whenever a lens is immersed in water/liquid, when designing lenses with specified radii of curvature, or when examining nature changes across media.
MASTER FORMULA
f1​=(μm​μL​​−1)(R1​1​−R2​1​)
Exam Strategy: Use the universal immersion ratio fa​fm​​=μL​−μm​(μL​−1)μm​​. For the specific condition μg​=1.5 in water μw​=4/3, this ratio evaluates to 4.0. For any other medium, evaluate the formula directly.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • μL​: Refractive index of lens material (glass typically 1.5=23​)
  • μm​: Refractive index of surrounding medium (air =1, water =34​)
  • R1​: Radius of first surface (R1​>0 if center of curvature lies to the right)
  • R2​: Radius of second surface (R2​<0 if center of curvature lies to the left for biconvex)

One-Step Derived Forms

Focal length ratio in medium vs air
fmfa=(μL−1)μmμL−μm\frac{f_m}{f_a} = \frac{(\mu_L - 1)\mu_m}{\mu_L - \mu_m}fa​fm​​=μL​−μm​(μL​−1)μm​​

Ratio formed by dividing Lens Maker formula in air by formula in medium. For crown glass in water: 1.5−4/3(1.5−1)(4/3)​=1/62/3​=4.0.

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Lens immersed in liquid / water” ⟹ Apply fa​fm​​=μL​−μm​(μL​−1)μm​​. Multiply by 4 if glass in water.
  • ▸ “Lens becomes invisible in a liquid” ⟹μm​=μL​ (f→∞).
  • ▸ “Air bubble inside water” ⟹ Diverging lens (f<0).

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Equiconvex Lens in Air (R1 = +R, R2 = -R) Verified PYQ
f1​=(μ−1)R2​⟹f=2(μ−1)R​

Condition: For glass with μ=1.5=23​: f=R exactly!

Physics Rule: For equiconcave lens: f=−2(μ−1)R​. When μ=1.5, f=−R.

Plano-Convex Lens in Air (R1 = R, R2 = infinity) Verified PYQ
f1​=Rμ−1​⟹f=μ−1R​

Condition: One curved surface of radius R, one flat plane surface (R2​→∞).

Physics Rule: For μ=1.5: f=2R (focal length is double that of equiconvex lens of the same radius).

Three Critical Regimes of Surrounding Medium Verified PYQ
⎩⎨⎧​μm​<μL​μm​=μL​μm​>μL​​Nature unchanged, ∣fm​∣>∣fa​∣fm​→∞, behaves as flat plate (invisible)Nature REVERSES! Convex becomes diverging​

Condition: Comparison between surrounding medium index μm​ and lens index μL​.

Physics Rule: Air bubble in water (μL​=1,μm​=34​): behaves as a DIVERGING lens despite convex physical geometry!

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Flat glass plate limit (R1​→∞,R2​→∞):
f1​=(μ−1)(0−0)=0⟹f→∞,P=0
No convergence or divergence; rays pass straight through.
Surrounding medium index matches lens (μm​=μL​):
μm​μL​​−1=0⟹f1​=0⟹f→∞
Lens disappears inside liquid; acts as homogeneous continuous medium.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Forgetting μm​ in the relative index: writing (μL​−1) instead of (μm​μL​​−1).
  • ⚠ Sign error for R2​ in equiconvex: R2​ is measured against light direction, so R2​=−R. Giving R1​1​−R2​1​=R1​−(−R1​)=+R2​.
  • ⚠ When lens is in a medium, power Pm​=fm​1​. If fw​=4fa​, then Pw​=4Pa​​.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A convex lens of focal length 24 cm made of glass (μg​=1.5) is completely immersed in water (μw​=4/3). Find the new focal length and optical power in water.

Given Data: fa​=24 cm,μg​=1.5=23​,μw​=34​

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Calculate immersion ratio: fa​fw​​=μg​−μw​(μg​−1)μw​​.
  2. Numerator: (1.5−1)×34​=0.5×34​=32​.
  3. Denominator: 1.5−34​=23​−34​=61​.
  4. Ratio: fa​fw​​=1/62/3​=4.0.
  5. Calculate fw​: fw​=4×24 cm=96 cm=0.96 m.
  6. Calculate power: Pw​=0.961​≈+1.04 D (which is Pa​/4=4.17/4).
Final Answer: fw​=96 cm,Pw​=+1.04 D

Module 3: Cutting of Lenses: Vertical, Horizontal & Quadrant Splits

High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2023, 2025, 2026

Exact physical laws governing focal length f′, power P′, and image brightness I′ when a lens is cut along or perpendicular to its optical axis.

When to Use It: Use when questions ask about splitting a lens into halves, covering parts of a lens aperture, or creating multi-image Billet split lens configurations.
MASTER FORMULA
Vertical: f′=2f,P′=2P​,I′=I;Horizontal: f′=f,P′=P,I′=2I​
Exam Strategy: Vertical cut changes curvature (f doubles). Horizontal cut only chops aperture area (f unchanged, intensity I drops).

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • f: Original focal length of intact symmetric biconvex lens
  • P: Original optical power (P=f1​)
  • I: Original image brightness / intensity (proportional to aperture area A∝D2)

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Lens cut along principal axis (horizontal)” ⟹f′=f, power unchanged, intensity halved (I/2).
  • ▸ “Lens cut perpendicular to principal axis (vertical)” ⟹f′=2f, power halved (P/2), intensity full (I).
  • ▸ “Central circular aperture of diameter D/2 is blackened” ⟹ Full image still formed; intensity becomes I′=I(1−1/4)=3I/4.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Case 1: Cut perpendicular to Principal Axis (Vertical Cut) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2025 April (Biconvex cut into parts)
f′=2f,P′=2P​,I′=I

Condition: Symmetric biconvex lens (f) cut along its aperture plane into two plano-convex halves.

Physics Rule: Each half has R1​=R,R2​=∞. Hence f′1​=Rμ−1​=2f1​⟹f′=2f. Intensity remains I′=I because the full aperture diameter still collects light.

Case 2: Cut parallel to Principal Axis (Horizontal Cut) Verified PYQ
f′=f,P′=P,I′=2I​

Condition: Cut along the optical axis into upper and lower halves.

Physics Rule: Curvature radii R1​,R2​ and refractive index μ are completely unchanged, so f′=f! But aperture area is halved, so image intensity I′=2I​.

Case 3: Cut into 4 equal quadrants (Vertical + Horizontal) High-Value Variation
f′=2f,P′=2P​,I′=4I​

Condition: One cut along optical axis, one cut perpendicular to optical axis.

Physics Rule: Each quadrant acts as a plano-convex lens with double focal length (2f) and one-fourth image brightness (4I​).

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Putting cut vertical halves back-to-back (d=0):
F1​=2f1​+2f1​=f1​
Reconstructs original focal length f.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Assuming that cutting along the principal axis doubles focal length: WRONG! Curvature is untouched, so f′=f.
  • ⚠ Forgetting that intensity depends on aperture area (4πD2​). If central circular zone of diameter 2D​ is blacked out: ΔI=I(1−41​)=43I​.
  • ⚠ Missing that a complete image is STILL formed when half the lens is covered; only brightness drops by half.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: An equiconvex lens of focal length f=20 cm and power +5 D forming an image of intensity I is cut into two equal halves along its principal axis. What are the focal length, power, and image intensity of each half?

Given Data: f=20 cm,P=+5 D,Cut: Horizontal (along principal axis)

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Analyze curvature: Cutting horizontally along the principal axis leaves both surface radii R1​ and R2​ identical to the original lens.
  2. Apply Lens Maker equation: Since R1​,R2​ and μ are unchanged, the focal length is unchanged: f′=f=20 cm.
  3. Calculate power: P′=f′1​=+5 D.
  4. Analyze intensity: The light-collecting area of each half is exactly half the original aperture area: A′=A/2. Hence intensity is I′=I/2.
Final Answer: f′=20 cm,P′=+5 D,I′=I/2

Module 4: Combinations of Thin Lenses: Contact & Separated Systems

Extreme Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026

Formulates equivalent focal length Feq​, power Peq​, and magnification for thin lenses touching or separated by axial distance d.

When to Use It: Use when multiple lenses are placed touching in contact or separated by distance d along a common optical axis.
MASTER FORMULA
Feq​1​=f1​1​+f2​1​−f1​f2​d​,Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​
Exam Strategy: For power in Diopters: Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​; always convert f and d to meters before calculating power.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • f1​,f2​: Focal lengths of individual lenses with Cartesian signs
  • d: Axial separation between lenses (MUST be in meters for power in Diopters!)
  • Peq​: Equivalent power: Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​
  • meq​: Total linear magnification: meq​=m1​×m2​

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Two thin lenses in contact” ⟹P=P1​+P2​ and 1/F=1/f1​+1/f2​.
  • ▸ “Two lenses separated by distance d” ⟹ Use P=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​ with d in METERS.
  • ▸ “Achromatic combination in contact” ⟹ω1​/f1​+ω2​/f2​=0.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Thin Lenses in Contact (d = 0) Verified PYQ
Feq​1​=i∑​fi​1​,Peq​=i∑​Pi​

Condition: Lenses touching with negligible gap (d=0).

Physics Rule: If convex (f1​=+20 cm) and concave (f2​=−30 cm) in contact: F1​=201​−301​=601​⟹F=+60 cm (converging).

Two Lenses Separated by Distance d Verified PYQ JEE Main 2025 April (f1​=30 cm,f2​=10 cm,d=10 cm⟹Peq​=+10 D)
Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​⟺Feq​1​=f1​1​+f2​1​−f1​f2​d​

Condition: Parallel beam of light incident on combination separated by distance d.

Physics Rule: If d=f1​+f2​: parallel beam emerges parallel (afocal system, Feq​→∞,Peq​=0).

Achromatic Doublet in Contact (Zero Chromatic Aberration) Verified PYQ
f1​ω1​​+f2​ω2​​=0⟹f2​f1​​=−ω2​ω1​​

Condition: Two lenses of different materials in contact to eliminate longitudinal chromatic aberration.

Physics Rule: Since ω>0 for all real materials, f1​ and f2​ MUST HAVE OPPOSITE SIGNS (one convex, one concave).

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Contact limit (d→0):
Peq​=P1​+P2​
Direct linear sum of Diopters.
Afocal separation (d=f1​+f2​):
Feq​1​=f1​1​+f2​1​−f1​f2​f1​+f2​​=0⟹Peq​=0
System has infinite focal length; incoming parallel beam emerges parallel.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Applying P=P1​+P2​ when lenses are separated by distance d: MUST use P=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​ with d in METERS if P is in Diopters!
  • ⚠ Unit mismatch trap: if f1​,f2​ are in cm, convert d to cm when using F1​=f1​1​+f2​1​−f1​f2​d​. If using P in Diopters, d MUST be in meters.
  • ⚠ Sign error with virtual object: if image I1​ is 10 cm behind lens 2, u2​=+10 cm, NOT −10 cm.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: Two convex lenses of focal lengths f1​=30 cm and f2​=10 cm are aligned coaxially separated by a distance d=10 cm. Find the equivalent optical power of the combination in Diopters.

Given Data: f1​=0.3 m⟹P1​=+310​ D,f2​=0.1 m⟹P2​=+10 D,d=10 cm=0.1 m

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Convert focal lengths to individual powers: P1​=0.31​=310​ D, P2​=0.11​=10 D.
  2. State the separated lens power equation: Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​.
  3. Substitute with d in meters (0.1 m): Peq​=310​+10−(0.1)(310​)(10).
  4. Simplify product term: (0.1)×10×310​=1×310​=310​.
  5. Combine terms: Peq​=310​+10−310​=10 D.
Final Answer: Peq​=+10 D

Module 5: Silvered Lenses: Equivalent Curved Mirror Master Equations

Very High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2024, 2025, 2026

When one face of a lens is silvered, light undergoes refraction into the lens, reflection at the rear mirror boundary, and refraction exiting the lens.

When to Use It: Use whenever a lens surface is coated with silver or placed in contact with a mirror to find image position or focal length.
MASTER FORMULA
Peq​=2PL​+PM​,Feq​=−Peq​1​
Exam Strategy: Always write Peq​=2PL​+PM​, set Feq​=−Peq​1​, and solve using standard MIRROR equation v1​+u1​=Feq​1​.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • PL​: Power of the refracting lens surface(s): PL​=fL​1​
  • PM​: Power of the reflecting mirror surface (PM​=−fM​1​=+R2​ for concave reflection)
  • Peq​: Equivalent power of the optical system: Peq​=2PL​+PM​
  • Feq​: Equivalent focal length; system ALWAYS acts as a spherical MIRROR (Feq​=−Peq​1​)

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Plano-convex lens silvered on flat face” ⟹ Concave mirror of Feq​=−2(μ−1)R​. If μ=1.5, Feq​=−R.
  • ▸ “Plano-convex lens silvered on curved face” ⟹ Concave mirror of Feq​=−2μR​. If μ=1.5, Feq​=−R/3.
  • ▸ “Silvered lens forms image at object position” ⟹u=2Feq​ (object at Center of Curvature of equivalent mirror).

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Plano-Convex Lens Silvered on Curved Face Verified PYQ JEE Main 2025 & 2026 Jan
PL​=Rμ−1​,PM​=R2​⟹Peq​=R2μ​⟹Feq​=−2μR​

Condition: Light incident on flat surface, reflects off curved back face.

Physics Rule: Acts as a CONCAVE MIRROR of focal length 2μR​. For μ=1.5, Feq​=−3R​.

Plano-Convex Lens Silvered on Flat Plane Face Verified PYQ JEE Main 2024 & 2025
PL​=Rμ−1​,PM​=0⟹Peq​=R2(μ−1)​⟹Feq​=−2(μ−1)R​

Condition: Curved surface faces the object; flat rear face is silvered (RM​→∞⟹PM​=0).

Physics Rule: For μ=1.5: Feq​=−R. Acts as a concave mirror of focal length R.

Equiconvex Lens Silvered on One Face Verified PYQ
PL​=R2(μ−1)​,PM​=R2​⟹Peq​=R4μ−2​⟹Feq​=−4μ−2R​

Condition: Symmetric biconvex lens of radius R with one face silvered.

Physics Rule: For μ=1.5: Peq​=R6−2​=R4​⟹Feq​=−4R​. Focal length is 4R​.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Flat glass slab silvered on back (R→∞):
PL​=0,PM​=0⟹Peq​=0,Feq​→∞
Behaves as ordinary plane mirror with apparent depth shift.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Forgetting that a silvered lens acts as a MIRROR, NOT a lens! Therefore use mirror formula v1​+u1​=Feq​1​.
  • ⚠ Sign trap: In mirrors, Concave Mirror has P>0 and F<0. That is why Feq​=−Peq​1​.
  • ⚠ Failure to double the lens power: light passes through the lens TWICE (forward and backward), so 2PL​ is mandatory.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A plano-convex lens of radius of curvature R=30 cm and refractive index μ=1.5 has its plane surface silvered. An object is placed at a distance of 40 cm in front of the curved surface. Find the position of the final image.

Given Data: R=30 cm,μ=1.5,Silvered: Plane face,u=−40 cm

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Calculate lens power: PL​=Rμ−1​=0.301.5−1​=0.300.5​=+35​ D.
  2. Silvered flat surface has RM​=∞⟹PM​=0.
  3. Total equivalent power: Peq​=2PL​+PM​=2(35​)+0=+310​ D.
  4. Equivalent focal length: Feq​=−Peq​1​=−103​ m=−30 cm (Concave mirror!).
  5. Apply mirror formula: v1​+u1​=Feq​1​⟹v1​−401​=−301​.
  6. Solve for v: v1​=−301​+401​=120−4+3​=−1201​⟹v=−120 cm.
Final Answer: v=−120 cm (Real image 120 cm in front of the curved surface)

Module 6: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces & Curved Interfaces

Very High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026

The fundamental equation for light passing from medium 1 (μ1​) to medium 2 (μ2​) across a spherical boundary of radius R.

When to Use It: Use for single curved glass boundaries, glass spheres, cylinders, air bubbles in glass, or liquid surfaces.
MASTER FORMULA
vμ2​​−uμ1​​=Rμ2​−μ1​​
Exam Strategy: Write "light in μ1​→ strikes surface R→ goes into μ2​". Use m=μ2​uμ1​v​ every time.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • μ1​: Refractive index of medium containing the incident ray
  • μ2​: Refractive index of medium containing the refracted ray
  • u,v: Object and image distances measured from pole of curved surface
  • R: Radius of curvature (R>0 if center lies in medium 2, i.e. along ray direction)
  • m: Lateral magnification: m=ho​hi​​=μ2​uμ1​v​

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Glass sphere of radius R, incident parallel rays” ⟹ Two refractions: 1st surface followed by 2nd surface.
  • ▸ “Air bubble inside glass sphere” ⟹μ1​=μglass​,μ2​=1,R<0.
  • ▸ “Magnification of spherical surface” ⟹m=μ2​uμ1​v​.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Lateral Magnification Formula (Crucial mu Factor!) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2025 April
m=ho​hi​​=μ2​uμ1​v​

Condition: Valid for all single curved refracting boundaries.

Physics Rule: Notice the ratio μ2​μ1​​! It is NOT simply uv​.

Air Bubble inside Glass Sphere (Radius R, Index mu) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2024 & 2025
v1​−uμ​=−R1−μ​

Condition: Light travels from glass (μ1​=μ) into air (μ2​=1). Surface is concave towards incident light (R=−R).

Physics Rule: If bubble is at the center: u=−R⟹v=−R (image formed at the center itself, unaffected by refraction).

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Flat plane boundary limit (R→∞):
vμ2​​−uμ1​​=0⟹v=μ1​μ2​​u
Directly reproduces apparent depth equation dapp​=μrel​d​.
Object at center of curvature (u=−R with R>0):
vμ2​​−−Rμ1​​=Rμ2​−μ1​​⟹vμ2​​=Rμ2​​⟹v=−R
Image forms at the center itself without deviation (rays are normal to interface).

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Magnification trap: writing m=uv​ instead of m=μ2​uμ1​v​. NTA gives both options in MCQs!
  • ⚠ Swapping μ1​ and μ2​: μ1​ is ALWAYS where incident light originates; μ2​ is where light enters.
  • ⚠ Sign of R: If convex surface bulges towards the incoming light, R>0; if concave towards incoming light, R<0.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A solid glass sphere of radius R=10 cm and refractive index μ=1.5 has a small air bubble embedded 4 cm below the surface. Where does the bubble appear when viewed normally from outside?

Given Data: R=10 cm,μ1​=1.5 (glass),μ2​=1.0 (air),u=−4 cm

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Identify geometry: Light travels from inside the glass (μ1​=1.5) to air outside (μ2​=1.0).
  2. Curvature sign: The sphere surface is concave toward the bubble inside, so R=−10 cm.
  3. Apply surface equation: vμ2​​−uμ1​​=Rμ2​−μ1​​.
  4. Substitute: v1.0​−−41.5​=−101.0−1.5​⟹v1​+83​=−10−0.5​=+201​.
  5. Solve for 1/v: v1​=201​−83​=402−15​=−4013​⟹v=−1340​≈−3.08 cm.
Final Answer: v=−3.08 cm (Appears 3.08 cm below surface)

Module 7: Plane Refraction, Apparent Depth & Parallel Slab Shifts

Very High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025

Exact formulas for apparent depth, normal optical shift by parallel plate, lateral beam displacement, and optical path length.

When to Use It: Use for objects viewed through water, layered immiscible liquids, glass slabs inserted before lenses/mirrors, or optical path calculations.
MASTER FORMULA
dapp​=μd​,Δt=t(1−μ1​),x=cosrtsin(i−r)​
Exam Strategy: Treat a slab simply as a device that displaces the object forward towards the observer by Δt=t(1−μ1​).

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • d: Real depth in optically denser medium
  • dapp​: Apparent depth observed from rarer medium: dapp​=μrel​d​
  • t: Thickness of parallel refracting slab
  • Δt: Normal shift of image towards observer: Δt=t(1−μ1​)
  • x: Lateral displacement (perpendicular shift of ray after traversing slab)

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Tank filled with two immiscible liquids” ⟹dapp​=μ1​d1​​+μ2​d2​​.
  • ▸ “Glass slab inserted between object and lens” ⟹ Shift object towards lens by Δt=t(1−1/μ).
  • ▸ “Observer in water looks at bird in air” ⟹ Bird appears HIGHER at happ​=μh.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Apparent Depth in Multiple Immiscible Liquids (Near-Normal Viewing) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2023 & 2024 Jan
dapp​=i=1∑n​μi​di​​=μ1​d1​​+μ2​d2​​+⋯+μn​dn​​

Condition: Parallel horizontal layers of liquids stacked in a vessel, observed strictly under near-normal (paraxial) viewing from air. For oblique viewing, Snell's law must be evaluated at each boundary.

Physics Rule: Total normal apparent shift: Δd=∑di​(1−μi​1​). You CANNOT use the arithmetic or weighted average of refractive indices!

Normal Shift Invariance by Glass Slab Verified PYQ
Δt=t(1−μ1​)[INDEPENDENT OF SLAB POSITION]

Condition: A flat glass slab placed anywhere between an object and a lens/mirror.

Physics Rule: Effective object distance becomes ueff​=u−Δt. The exact location of the slab between object and lens does not matter!

Lateral Displacement for Small Angles of Incidence Verified PYQ JEE Main 2024 April (t=43​ cm at critical angle)
x≈t⋅i(1−μ1​)

Condition: Angle of incidence i is small (paraxial rays).

Physics Rule: Maximum lateral displacement as i→90∘ is xmax​=t.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Air slab (μ=1):
Δt=t(1−1)=0,dapp​=d
No shift or displacement.
Very high refractive index (μ→∞):
Δt→t,dapp​→0
Image appears on the front surface of the slab.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Using average refractive index for multiple liquids: total apparent depth is SUM ∑μi​di​​, NOT μˉ​∑di​​.
  • ⚠ Confusing normal shift with apparent depth: apparent depth is μd​, but normal shift is t(1−μ1​).
  • ⚠ Thinking that sliding the glass slab closer to the lens changes the focus: the shift Δt is strictly independent of where the slab sits along the optical path!

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A vessel contains two immiscible liquids: a bottom layer of depth d1​=9 cm with μ1​=1.5, and an upper layer of depth d2​=8 cm with μ2​=4/3. Find the apparent depth of the bottom of the vessel as seen from above.

Given Data: d1​=9 cm,μ1​=1.5=23​,d2​=8 cm,μ2​=34​

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Apply multi-layer superposition: dapp​=μ1​d1​​+μ2​d2​​.
  2. Calculate layer 1 contribution: 1.59​=6 cm.
  3. Calculate layer 2 contribution: 4/38​=8×43​=6 cm.
  4. Sum the apparent depths: dapp​=6 cm+6 cm=12 cm.
  5. Total physical depth is 9+8=17 cm. The apparent shift is Δd=17−12=5 cm.
Final Answer: dapp​=12 cm(Apparent shift =5 cm)

Module 8: Total Internal Reflection, Critical Angle & Optical Fiber

Very High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2024, 2026

Condition for total internal reflection when light travels from an optically denser medium into a rarer medium.

When to Use It: Use whenever calculating critical angle, fish-eye illuminated circle on liquid surface, optical fiber acceptance cone, or Porro prism reflections.
MASTER FORMULA
sinC=μd​μr​​=vr​vd​​=λr​λd​​
Exam Strategy: Whenever speeds v1​,v2​ are given: sinC=v2​v1​​ where v1​<v2​. Always smaller speed over larger speed.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • C: Critical angle: angle of incidence in denser medium for which refraction angle is 90∘
  • μd​,μr​: Refractive indices of denser and rarer media (μd​>μr​)
  • vd​,vr​: Speed of light in denser and rarer media (vd​<vr​)

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Speeds of light in two media are v1​,v2​” ⟹sinC=vsmaller​/vlarger​.
  • ▸ “Point source at depth h in water; find circular illuminated area” ⟹A=μ2−1πh2​.
  • ▸ “Numerical Aperture of optical fiber” ⟹NA=μcore2​−μclad2​​.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Critical Angle from Speeds of Light (NTA Favorite) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2026 Jan (v1​=1.5×108,v2​=2.0×108⟹sinC=43​)
sinC=v2​v1​​(v1​<v2​)

Condition: When question specifies speeds of light in two media without explicitly stating μ.

Physics Rule: Always smaller speed over larger speed: sinC=vrarer​vdenser​​.

Circle of Illuminance (Fish-Eye Horizon) Verified PYQ
r=htanC=μ2−1​h​,Area A=μ2−1πh2​

Condition: Point source of light at depth h below liquid surface of index μ.

Physics Rule: Light emerges into air only through this circular cone of apex angle 2C.

Optical Fiber Acceptance Angle & Numerical Aperture Verified PYQ
sinθmax​=μcore2​−μclad2​​≡NA

Condition: Maximum incident angle θmax​ at the fiber entrance face for TIR to occur at core-cladding interface.

Physics Rule: Condition for light incident at ANY angle (θmax​≥90∘) to suffer TIR: μcore​≥μclad2​+1​.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Equal media (μd​=μr​):
sinC=1⟹C=90∘
TIR impossible, no boundary exists.
Extreme index contrast (μd​≫μr​):
C→0∘
Almost all rays undergo total internal reflection (like diamond: C≈24.4∘).

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Applying TIR when going from rarer to denser: TIR is IMPOSSIBLE if μincident​<μrefracted​.
  • ⚠ Inverting the ratio: sinC≤1 always, so it is strictly μdenser​μrarer​​=vrarer​vdenser​​.
  • ⚠ For optical fiber: forgetting that refractive index of core must be GREATER than cladding (μcore​>μclad​).

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: The speed of light in two media A and B are 1.5×108 m/s and 2.0×108 m/s respectively. Find the critical angle for total internal reflection between the two media.

Given Data: vA​=1.5×108 m/s,vB​=2.0×108 m/s

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Identify denser and rarer: Medium A has lower speed, so it is optically denser (μA​>μB​).
  2. TIR occurs for rays originating in medium A heading toward medium B.
  3. State formula: sinC=vrarer​vdenser​​=vB​vA​​.
  4. Substitute: sinC=2.0×1081.5×108​=2.01.5​=43​=0.75.
  5. Critical angle: C=sin−1(0.75)≈48.6∘.
Final Answer: sinC=43​⟹C=sin−1(0.75)

Module 9: Prisms, Minimum Deviation, Dispersion & Achromatic Systems

Very High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026

Master prism equations covering general refraction, condition of minimum deviation, thin prisms, and dispersion relations.

When to Use It: Use for ray tracing in prisms, minimum deviation questions, critical angle grazing emergence, and achromatic or direct-vision prism pairs.
MASTER FORMULA
A=r1​+r2​,δ=i+e−A,μ=sin(2A​)sin(2A+δm​​)​
Exam Strategy: First check if the question states "minimum deviation"; if so, immediately write r1​=r2​=2A​ and i=2A+δm​​.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • A: Angle of prism (refracting angle)
  • i,e: Angle of incidence and angle of emergence
  • r1​,r2​: Refraction angles at first and second surfaces (r1​+r2​=A)
  • δm​: Minimum deviation: occurs when i=e and r1​=r2​=2A​

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Minimum deviation” ⟹r1​=r2​=A/2 and i=e=(A+δm​)/2.
  • ▸ “Ray emerges along the surface (grazing emergence)” ⟹e=90∘⟹r2​=C=sin−1(1/μ).
  • ▸ “No light can emerge from prism for any angle of incidence” ⟹A>2C.
  • ▸ “Dispersion without deviation” ⟹ Net deviation (μy​−1)A+(μy′​−1)A′=0.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Condition for Minimum Deviation (Symmetry) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2024, 2025, 2026 Jan
i=e,r1​=r2​=2A​⟹μ=sin(2A​)sin(2A+δm​​)​

Condition: Ray passes symmetrically through prism parallel to base.

Physics Rule: If A=60∘ and μ=3​: sin(260∘+δm​​)=3​sin(30∘)=23​​⟹δm​=60∘.

Condition for No Emergence (TIR at Second Face for All Incidences) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2026 Jan
A>2θc​⟹TIR occurs at second face for ALL angles of incidence i∈[0,90∘]

Condition: Maximum refraction angle at face 1 is r1,max​=θc​ (at grazing incidence i=90∘). Hence r2​=A−r1​≥A−θc​>θc​ for all i if A>2θc​.

Physics Rule: Condition for light to be capable of emerging: A≤2θc​. The minimum incidence angle for emergence is imin​=sin−1(μsin(A−θc​)).

Two Combination Modes: Achromatic vs Direct Vision Verified PYQ JEE Main 2026 Jan
{Deviation without Dispersion: Dispersion without Deviation: ​A′=−μv′​−μr′​μv​−μr​​AA′=−μy′​−1μy​−1​A​

Condition: Prisms placed in opposite orientations.

Physics Rule: JEE Main 2026 Jan specifically tested Dispersion without Deviation (Direct Vision Spectroscope)!

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Thin prism (A≤10∘):
δ≈(μ−1)A
Deviation is independent of incidence angle for paraxial rays.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Assuming r1​=r2​ always: r1​=r2​=2A​ ONLY at minimum deviation! In general, r1​+r2​=A.
  • ⚠ Assuming dispersive power depends on prism angle A: ω=μy​−1μv​−μr​​ is an intrinsic material property independent of A.
  • ⚠ At minimum deviation, the ray inside the prism is PARALLEL to the base ONLY for an isosceles or equilateral prism.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A ray of light is incident at minimum deviation on an equilateral glass prism of refractive index μ=3​. Find the angle of incidence i and angle of minimum deviation δm​.

Given Data: A=60∘,μ=3​

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. At minimum deviation, internal angles are r1​=r2​=2A​=260∘​=30∘.
  2. Apply Snell's law at first surface: sini=μsinr1​=3​sin(30∘)=3​×21​=23​​.
  3. Solve for i: i=sin−1(23​​)=60∘.
  4. Calculate minimum deviation: δm​=2i−A=2(60∘)−60∘=60∘.
Final Answer: i=60∘,δm​=60∘

Module 10: Spherical Mirrors, Newton's Formula & Image Velocities

High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2026

Concave and convex mirrors with Cartesian coordinate conventions, Newton focus distance formula, and velocity relations.

When to Use It: Use for reflection at curved surfaces, moving objects/mirrors along optical axis, or when distances are measured relative to the focus.
MASTER FORMULA
f1​=v1​+u1​,m=−uv​=f−uf​=ff−v​
Exam Strategy: Convex mirror always gives virtual diminished image for real objects (0<m<1). Use m=f−uf​ directly.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • f: Focal length: f=2R​. Concave: f<0. Convex: f>0.
  • u: Object distance (u<0 for real object)
  • v: Image distance (v<0 for real image, v>0 for virtual image)
  • m: Transverse magnification: m=−uv​

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Distances given from the focal point” ⟹x1​x2​=f2.
  • ▸ “Object moving along principal axis towards mirror” ⟹vI​=−m2vO​.
  • ▸ “Convex mirror forms image half the size” ⟹m=+1/2 (convex mirror image is always erect for real object).

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Instant Magnification Shortcuts (Eliminating u or v) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2024 (Convex mirror R=30 cm,m=+21​⟹u=−15 cm)
m=f−uf​=ff−v​

Condition: Avoids calculating v1​ first, directly relates size to u or v.

Physics Rule: For convex mirror (f>0) with real object (u<0): m=f+∣u∣f​⟹0<m<1 ALWAYS (virtual, erect, diminished).

Newton's Formula for Spherical Mirrors Verified PYQ
x1​⋅x2​=f2

Condition: x1​ and x2​ are distances of object and image measured FROM THE FOCUS (F), NOT the pole!

Physics Rule: Magnification: m=−fx2​​=−x1​f​. If x1​,x2​ are given from focus, solves the question in 3 seconds.

Longitudinal Magnification & Image Velocity High-Value Variation
mL​=−m2=−(uv​)2,vI,∥​=−m2vO,∥​

Condition: Small object moving parallel to principal axis with speed vO,∥​.

Physics Rule: Minus sign indicates that image moves in the opposite direction to object along the principal axis!

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Object at center of curvature (u=−2f for concave):
v=−2f,m=−1
Real inverted image at the same position and same size.
Flat plane mirror limit (R→∞):
f→∞⟹v=−u,m=+1
Standard plane reflection.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Magnification sign: mirror has MINUS: m=−uv​, whereas lens has m=+uv​.
  • ⚠ Convex mirror image trap: For a real object, a convex mirror NEVER forms a real image or an enlarged image. If a question gives m=+2 for a convex mirror, the object MUST be virtual!
  • ⚠ Newton formula trap: x1​ and x2​ MUST be measured from the focal point F, NOT from pole P.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: A convex mirror has radius of curvature R=30 cm. At what distance should a real object be placed in front of it so that its image is diminished to half the size of the object?

Given Data: R=+30 cm⟹f=+15 cm,m=+21​

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Recognize magnification formula: m=f−uf​.
  2. Substitute m=+1/2 (since convex mirror forms erect virtual image of real object): 21​=15−u15​.
  3. Cross-multiply: 15−u=30.
  4. Solve for u: −u=30−15=15⟹u=−15 cm.
Final Answer: u=−15 cm (Object placed 15 cm in front of mirror)

Module 11: Plane Mirrors: Ray Rotation, Mirror Translation & Images

Medium Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2023

Exact geometric laws governing reflection from moving or inclined plane mirrors.

When to Use It: Use for rotating mirror galvanometers, plane mirrors translating toward/away from objects, and counting images formed by two inclined mirrors.
MASTER FORMULA
Δθray​=2θmirror​,Δximage​=2Δxmirror​
Exam Strategy: Remember the factor of 2: mirror rotates θ⟹ ray rotates 2θ; mirror translates x⟹ image translates 2x.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • θmirror​: Angle by which mirror is rotated about axis in its plane
  • Δxmirror​: Displacement of plane mirror towards/away from object
  • n: Number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at angle θ

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Plane mirror rotated by θ keeping incident ray fixed” ⟹ Reflected ray turns by 2θ.
  • ▸ “Plane mirror moves towards stationary object at speed v” ⟹ Image moves at speed 2v.
  • ▸ “Number of images for angle θ” ⟹ Calculate 360∘/θ; if even, answer is 360∘/θ−1.

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Rotation of Mirror vs Reflected Ray Verified PYQ
Mirror rotates by θ⟹Reflected ray rotates by 2θ

Condition: Incident ray direction kept fixed.

Physics Rule: If incident ray also rotates by α in same sense, reflected ray rotates by 2θ−α.

Translation of Plane Mirror Verified PYQ JEE Main 2023 Shift 1
Δximage​=2Δxmirror​

Condition: Object is stationary; mirror moves towards object by distance x.

Physics Rule: Image moves by 2x towards object. Separation between object and image decreases by 2x.

Number of Images Formed by Two Inclined Mirrors Verified PYQ
n=⎩⎨⎧​θ360∘​−1θ360∘​−1θ360∘​​if θ360∘​ is EVEN (any object position)if θ360∘​ is ODD and object is on angle bisectorif θ360∘​ is ODD and object is ASYMMETRIC​

Condition: Two plane mirrors inclined at angle θ.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Parallel mirrors (θ=0∘):
n=0360∘​→∞
Infinite series of images arranged along perpendicular line.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Assuming image moves with same speed as mirror: if mirror moves at speed v towards object, image moves at speed 2v!
  • ⚠ Forgetting symmetric vs asymmetric condition for odd θ360∘​.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: Two plane mirrors are inclined at an angle of θ=72∘. Find the number of images formed for an object placed: (a) on the angle bisector, (b) off the angle bisector.

Given Data: θ=72∘⟹θ360∘​=72∘360∘​=5(ODD INTEGER)

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. Calculate ratio: 72∘360∘​=5. Since 5 is an ODD integer, image count depends on object position.
  2. Case (a) On angle bisector (symmetric): n=θ360∘​−1=5−1=4 images.
  3. Case (b) Off angle bisector (asymmetric): n=θ360∘​=5 images.
Final Answer: (a) 4 images, (b) 5 images

Module 12: Optical Instruments: Microscopes, Telescopes & Resolving Power

High Frequency Verified PYQ PYQs: 2022, 2024, 2026

Magnifying power and tube length formulas for simple microscope, compound microscope, and astronomical telescope.

When to Use It: Use for solving magnification, focal lengths, and tube lengths of compound microscopes and astronomical telescopes in normal adjustment or near point adjustment.
MASTER FORMULA
Mtele​=−fe​fo​​,Mmicro​≈−fo​L​⋅fe​D​
Exam Strategy: For telescope: system of 2 equations: M=fe​fo​​ and L=fo​+fe​ gives fo​ and fe​ instantly.

Symbol Definitions & Conventions

  • fo​,fe​: Objective and eyepiece focal lengths (fo​≫fe​ for telescope; fo​≪fe​ for microscope)
  • D: Least distance of distinct vision (standard D=25 cm=0.25 m)
  • L: Tube length: separation between objective and eyepiece
  • M: Angular magnification / magnifying power

Question Recognition Clues

  • ▸ “Telescope in normal adjustment” ⟹M=fo​/fe​ and L=fo​+fe​.
  • ▸ “Telescope image at near point D” ⟹M=fe​fo​​(1+fe​/D).
  • ▸ “Compound microscope” ⟹M=(uo​vo​​)(fe​D​).

All Important Variations & Edge Conditions

Astronomical Telescope: Normal Adjustment (Image at Infinity) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2022 & 2026 Jan
M=−fe​fo​​,L=fo​+fe​

Condition: Final image formed at infinity; eyes relaxed.

Physics Rule: In JEE Main 2022: given L=105 cm,M=20⟹fo​+fe​=105,fo​=20fe​⟹21fe​=105⟹fe​=5 cm,fo​=100 cm.

Astronomical Telescope: Near Point Adjustment (Image at D = 25 cm) High-Value Variation
M=−fe​fo​​(1+Dfe​​),L=fo​+ue​=fo​+fe​+Dfe​D​

Condition: Final image formed at least distance of distinct vision D.

Compound Microscope: Normal Adjustment (Image at Infinity) Verified PYQ JEE Main 2026 Jan
M=mo​×me​=(uo​vo​​)(fe​D​)≈−fo​L​⋅fe​D​

Condition: Final image at infinity; tube length L≈vo​.

Extreme-Case Sanity Checks (Limiting Boundaries)

Telescope normal adjustment (ve​→∞):
ue​=fe​,L=fo​+fe​
Maximum eye comfort with relaxed eye.

NTA Negative-Marking Traps to Avoid

  • ⚠ Inverting fo​ and fe​: In telescope, objective is huge: fo​≫fe​. In microscope, objective is tiny: fo​≪fe​.
  • ⚠ Normal adjustment means image at INFINITY (relaxed eye), NOT at 25 cm!
  • ⚠ Tube length in telescope: L=fo​+fe​ in normal adjustment; do not forget this direct relation to solve 2-variable systems.

Worked Archetype Problem & Attack System

Problem: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has a magnifying power of 20 and the distance between the objective and the eyepiece is 105 cm. Find the focal lengths of the objective and the eyepiece.

Given Data: M=20,L=105 cm,Normal adjustment

Step-by-Step Attack:
  1. In normal adjustment: M=fe​fo​​=20⟹fo​=20fe​.
  2. Tube length relation: L=fo​+fe​=105 cm.
  3. Substitute fo​: 20fe​+fe​=105⟹21fe​=105.
  4. Solve for fe​: fe​=21105​=5 cm.
  5. Solve for fo​: fo​=20×5=100 cm.
Final Answer: fo​=100 cm,fe​=5 cm
Section 2: “How to Attack the Question” Recognition Engine Instant Pattern Matching
Thin Lens
“Object placed at two positions gives same size images on screen / by lens”

Underlying Concept: Equal Magnification at Conjugate-like Positions

f=2u1​+u2​​orm1​=−m2​

Pitfall to Avoid: Do not set up two full lens equations and solve quadratics. One image is real (m=−k) and the other is virtual (m=+k).

PYQ Anchor: JEE Main 2026 Jan 28 Shift 1 (u1​=8 cm,u2​=24 cm⟹f=16 cm)

Lens Maker
“Lens immersed in water / liquid of refractive index μm​”

Underlying Concept: Relative Refractive Index Transformation

fa​fm​​=μL​−μm​(μL​−1)μm​​

Pitfall to Avoid: Never divide fa​ by μm​! Standard glass (μ=1.5) in water (μ=4/3) multiplies focal length by EXACTLY 4.

PYQ Anchor: JEE Main 2025 April Shift 1, 2026 Jan Shift 2

Silvered Lens
“One surface of plano-convex / equiconvex lens is silvered”

Underlying Concept: Equivalent Curved Mirror System (Peq​=2PL​+PM​)

Peq​v1​+u1​​=2PL​+PM​,Feq​=−Peq​1​=Feq​1​(System is Mirror!)​

Pitfall to Avoid: Never use lens formula v1​−u1​=f1​. A silvered lens is strictly a MIRROR (Feq​<0 for converging/concave mirror).

PYQ Anchor: JEE Main 2024 April Shift 2, 2025 Jan Shift 1, 2026 Jan Shift 1

Prisms & TIR
“Ray just suffers Total Internal Reflection / Grazing emergence at second surface”

Underlying Concept: Boundary Critical Angle Geometry (r2​=C=sin−1(1/μ))

r2​sini​=C=sin−1(1/μ),r1​=A−C=μsin(A−C)​

Pitfall to Avoid: Do not assume r1​=r2​. That only holds at minimum deviation! Here r2​ is pinned to critical angle C.

PYQ Anchor: JEE Main 2026 Jan 24 Shift 2, 2024 Jan 31 Shift 2

Prisms
“Condition for no ray to emerge from prism for ANY angle of incidence”

A>2Cwhere C=sin−1(μ1​)

Pitfall to Avoid: Even at grazing incidence (i=90∘), r1​=C, so r2​=A−C>C, guaranteeing internal reflection.

Prisms
“Prism at minimum deviation / Ray inside prism travels parallel to base”

Underlying Concept: Symmetric Refraction at Minimum Deviation

i=eμ​=2A+δm​​,r1​=r2​=2A​=sin(A/2)sin(2A+δm​​)​​

Pitfall to Avoid: Ray inside is parallel to the base ONLY if the prism is equilateral or isosceles with equal refracting faces.

Prisms & Dispersion
“Dispersion without deviation / Direct-Vision Spectroscope”

Underlying Concept: Net Mean Deviation Cancelled (δ1​+δ2​=0)

(μy​−1)A+(μy′​−1)A′=0⟹A′=−μy′​−1μy​−1​A

Pitfall to Avoid: Do not confuse with Achromatism (Deviation without dispersion, where net dispersion (μv​−μr​)A+(μv′​−μr′​)A′=0).

“Multiple immiscible liquids of depths d1​,d2​ in a container”

Underlying Concept: Linear Superposition of Apparent Depths

dapp​Δt​=i=1∑n​μi​di​​=μ1​d1​​+μ2​d2​​=i=1∑n​di​(1−μi​1​)​

Pitfall to Avoid: Never calculate an average refractive index μˉ​=2μ1​+μ2​​ or divide total depth by μˉ​.

Underlying Concept: Curvature Preservation vs Aperture Reduction

Vertical Cut: Horizontal Cut: ​f′=2f,P′=P/2,I′=If′=f,P′=P,I′=I/2​

sinC=v2​v1​​=vrarer​vdenser​​(v1​<v2​)

Mfe​​=fe​fo​​,L=fo​+fe​=M+1L​,fo​=M+1M⋅L​​

PYQ Anchor: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 2, 2025 Jan Shift 1

Section 4: Top 30 Negative-Marking Traps (NTA Pitfalls) Guaranteed Negative-Mark Saver

Immersion of Lens in Liquid (Water vs Air Multiplier) [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Dividing focal length by liquid index (fw​=fa​/1.33) or multiplying power by liquid index.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

fa​fm​​=μL​−μm​(μL​−1)μm​​. For standard glass (μL​=1.5) in water (μm​=4/3), fa​fw​​=4.0 exactly.

Why: Refractive power depends on relative refractive index (μm​μL​​−1), which drops dramatically from 0.5 to 0.125 (4× decrease in power).

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2025 April & 2026 Jan: Lens in air f=24 cm⟹fw​=96 cm.

Separated Lenses Power Equation & Unit Mismatch [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Calculating Peq​=P1​+P2​−dP1​P2​ with separation d in centimeters.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

If powers P1​,P2​ are in Diopters (m−1), separation d MUST be converted to METERS.

Why: Diopter is SI unit (1 D=1 m−1). Multiplying m−1×m−1×cm causes a 100× dimensional error.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2025 April Shift 2: f1​=30 cm,f2​=10 cm,d=10 cm⟹d=0.1 m⟹Peq​=+10 D.

Equal-Size Images at Two Object Positions [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Setting up two separate lens equations and attempting to solve a messy quadratic equation.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

f=2u1​+u2​​ when ∣m1​∣=∣m2​∣. One image is real (m=−k) and the other is virtual (m=+k).

Why: From m=f+uf​, setting −f+u1​f​=f+u2​f​ directly yields f+u1​=−(f+u2​)⟹2f=u1​+u2​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2026 Jan 28 Shift 1: u1​=8 cm,u2​=24 cm⟹f=16 cm in 5 seconds.

Silvered Lens Nature: Lens vs Mirror [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Treating the silvered system as a lens and using v1​−u1​=f1​.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

A silvered lens is ALWAYS an equivalent MIRROR. Use v1​+u1​=Feq​1​ with Feq​=−Peq​1​.

Why: Light reflects off the back coated surface, reversing its axial direction back into the original half-space.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 April Shift 2 & 2026 Jan Shift 1.

Multiple Immiscible Liquids Apparent Depth [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Averaging refractive indices: μˉ​=2μ1​+μ2​​ and writing dapp​=μˉ​d1​+d2​​.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

dapp​=∑i=1n​μi​di​​=μ1​d1​​+μ2​d2​​+⋯+μn​dn​​.

Why: Refraction occurs sequentially at each planar interface, summing individual optical delays linearly.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 Jan Shift 1 & 2024 April Shift 1.

Glass Slab Normal Shift Position Dependence [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming moving the glass slab closer to the lens or mirror changes the focal shift.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Δt=t(1−μ1​) is strictly INDEPENDENT of where the slab sits along the optical path.

Why: A parallel slab only displaces rays parallel to themselves by an invariant normal offset Δt.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2022 July & 2025 Jan Shift 2.

Cutting a Lens along Principal Axis (Horizontal Cut) [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Believing that cutting a lens horizontally in half doubles its focal length to 2f.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Focal length remains f′=f. Only image intensity drops by half (I′=I/2).

Why: Curvature radii R1​,R2​ and refractive index μ are unchanged, so 1/f=(μ−1)(1/R1​−1/R2​) is completely intact.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2025 April Shift 1 & 2023 Jan Shift 2.

Covering Central Half of Lens Aperture [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming only half of the image is formed, or that the center of the image vanishes.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

The ENTIRE image is formed intact at the same position. Only brightness decreases: I′=I(1−D2d2​).

Why: Every infinitesimal zone of the lens gathers rays from every point of the object and focuses them to the corresponding image point.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 April Shift 1.

Prism Ray Travel Parallel to Base Assumption [Tricky Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming ray inside prism is always parallel to the base at minimum deviation for any prism shape.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Ray inside is parallel to the base ONLY if the prism is equilateral or isosceles (A1​=A2​).

Why: Symmetry condition r1​=r2​=A/2 makes ray horizontal only relative to symmetric prism faces.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 1.

Dispersive Power Dependent on Prism Angle A [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Thinking a thicker prism or larger prism angle A gives higher dispersive power ω.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

ω=μy​−1μv​−μr​​ depends ONLY on the material, completely independent of angle A.

Why: Angular dispersion is (μv​−μr​)A and mean deviation is (μy​−1)A; the angle A cancels out in the ratio.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 April Shift 2 & 2026 Jan Shift 2.

Condition for No Emergence from Prism (A>2C) [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Checking whether i>C at first surface to predict emergence.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Ray cannot emerge for ANY incidence angle if A>2C where C=sin−1(1/μ).

Why: Maximum possible r1​ is C (at grazing incidence i=90∘), so minimum r2​=A−r1​=A−C>C, forcing TIR at second face.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2026 Jan 24 Shift 2 & 2023 April Shift 1.

Lateral Magnification at Curved Refracting Surface [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Writing magnification simply as m=uv​ as in thin lenses.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

m=μ2​uμ1​v​. Must include refractive index ratio μ2​μ1​​!

Why: Snell's law at curved pole: μ1​tanθ1​≈μ2​tanθ2​⟹μ1​uho​​=μ2​v−hi​​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2025 April Shift 2.

Air Bubble in Glass Sphere Refraction Signs [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Taking μ1​=1 and μ2​=1.5 and taking radius of curvature positive.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Light starts inside glass: μ1​=1.5,μ2​=1. The boundary is concave towards incoming light: R=−R.

Why: Rays emanate from the bubble inside glass, so glass is the incident medium μ1​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 2 & 2025 Jan Shift 1.

Convex Mirror Real Image Fallacy [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Expecting a convex mirror to form a real or magnified image for an object placed in front of it.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

For any REAL object, a convex mirror ALWAYS forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image (0<m<1).

Why: m=f−uf​. Since f>0 and u<0, denominator is f+∣u∣>f, making m strictly between 0 and 1.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 1: If m=+2 for convex mirror, object MUST be virtual (u>0).

Sign of Magnification: Mirror vs Lens [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Mixing up minus sign: writing m=+v/u for mirrors and m=−v/u for lenses.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Mirror: m=−uv​. Lens: m=+uv​.

Why: For a mirror, real image is on the same side (v<0,u<0⟹−v/u<0, inverted). For lens, real image is on opposite side (v>0,u<0⟹v/u<0).

PYQ Connection: Universal NTA sign trap across 2022–2026.

Newton's Formula Distance Reference [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Measuring x1​ and x2​ in x1​x2​=f2 from the pole/vertex of the mirror or lens.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

x1​ and x2​ MUST be measured from the FOCAL POINT F, not the pole.

Why: Newton's coordinates are centered at focus: u=−(f+x1​),v=−(f+x2​). Substituting into mirror formula yields x1​x2​=f2.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 April Shift 1.

Plane Mirror Translation vs Image Velocity [Tricky Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming if mirror moves with velocity vm​, the image moves with velocity vm​.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

With stationary object, image moves at vI​=2vm​. If mirror moves by x, image shifts by 2x.

Why: Distance from object to mirror equals distance from mirror to image; xI​=2xm​−xO​⟹dtdxI​​=2dtdxm​​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 Shift 1 & 2024 April Shift 2.

Plane Mirror Rotation vs Reflected Ray [Tricky Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Rotating mirror by angle θ rotates reflected ray by angle θ.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Reflected ray turns by angle 2θ (double the mirror rotation angle).

Why: Both angle of incidence i and normal shift by θ, adding θ+θ=2θ to ray deviation.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2022 June Shift 2.

Telescope Objective vs Eyepiece Focal Length Hierarchy [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Inverting fo​ and fe​, or assuming microscope and telescope have same design hierarchy.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Telescope: fo​≫fe​ (large objective for collecting light & high magnification M=fo​/fe​). Microscope: fo​≪fe​.

Why: Telescope magnifies distant objects (M=fo​/fe​), while microscope requires objective with huge initial linear magnification (vo​/uo​).

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2022 July & 2026 Jan Shift 2.

Normal Adjustment Meaning in Optical Instruments [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming normal adjustment means final image is at near point (D=25 cm).

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

“Normal Adjustment” means final image is at INFINITY (v=∞), giving relaxed eye condition.

Why: Ciliary eye muscles are completely relaxed only when receiving parallel rays from an image at infinity.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2022 July Shift 1, 2024 April Shift 2, 2026 Jan Shift 2.

TIR Directional Prerequisite [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Applying sinC=μ1​/μ2​ when light goes from air into glass.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

TIR is STRICTLY IMPOSSIBLE when light travels from rarer to denser medium. Denser → Rarer is mandatory.

Why: Ray bends away from normal only when entering a rarer medium (r>i), allowing r to reach 90∘.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 2.

Critical Angle from Light Speeds [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Dividing larger speed by smaller speed: writing sinC=v2​/v1​>1.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

sinC=v2​v1​​ where v1​<v2​ (vdenser​/vrarer​). Sine can NEVER exceed 1!

Why: Refractive index is inversely proportional to speed: μ=c/v, so sinC=μr​/μd​=vd​/vr​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2026 Jan 29 Shift 1: v1​=1.5×108,v2​=2.0×108⟹sinC=3/4.

Optical Fiber Acceptance Angle Formula [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Thinking sinθmax​=μcore​−μclad​ or inverting the terms.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

sinθmax​=μcore2​−μclad2​​≡NA.

Why: Snell's law at entrance: 1⋅sinθ=μ1​sinr=μ1​cosC=μ1​1−(μ2​/μ1​)2​=μ12​−μ22​​.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 Jan Shift 2 & 2025 April Shift 1.

Nature Reversal of Lens in Denser Liquid [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming a glass convex lens remains converging no matter what liquid it is immersed in.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

If liquid index exceeds lens index (μm​>μL​), nature REVERSES: convex lens becomes DIVERGING.

Why: In (μm​μL​​−1), if μm​>μL​, the bracket becomes NEGATIVE, flipping the sign of focal length.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 April Shift 1: Glass lens (μ=1.5) in liquid (μ=1.65).

Air Bubble in Water: Physical Geometry vs Optical Nature [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Assuming an spherical air bubble in water behaves as a converging lens because it is convex-shaped.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Air bubble in water behaves as a DIVERGING (concave) lens of focal length f=−2(μw​−1)R​.

Why: Here lens medium is air (μL​=1) and surrounding medium is water (μm​=4/3>μL​). Hence nature is diverging.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2022 June Shift 1 & 2025 Jan Shift 2.

Achromatic Doublet Lens Material Sign Requirement [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Attempting to build an achromatic doublet using two convex lenses of different materials in contact.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

f1​ω1​​+f2​ω2​​=0. Since ω1​,ω2​>0 for all real materials, one lens MUST be convex and one MUST be concave.

Why: To cancel positive chromatic dispersion of converging lens, a diverging lens with negative focal length is required.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 April Shift 1 & 2026 Jan Shift 1.

Minimum Object-to-Real-Image Distance for Convex Lens [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Believing a screen can be placed at any distance D from an object to catch a real image.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Screen separation D MUST be at least 4f (D≥4f). If D<4f, NO REAL IMAGE can be formed on the screen.

Why: From D=∣u∣+v, substituting v=u−fuf​ gives quadratic u2−Du+Df=0. Real roots require discriminant D2−4Df≥0⟹D≥4f.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 Jan Shift 2 & 2026 Jan Shift 2.

Longitudinal Magnification for Finite Object vs Small Element [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Using mL​=m2 for a finite rod of length 10 cm along the optical axis.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

mL​=m2 is valid ONLY for differential elements (du→0). For finite rod: MUST find v1​,v2​ separately and use L′=∣v2​−v1​∣.

Why: Magnification varies non-linearly across different points of an extended object along the axis.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2024 April Shift 1: Rod of length 5 cm on concave mirror axis.

Small Prism Deviation Angle Validity Range [High Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Applying δ=(μ−1)A to a 60∘ equilateral prism.

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

δ≈(μ−1)A is valid ONLY for thin prisms (A≤10∘). For 60∘, must use exact Snell's law.

Why: Derivation relies on small-angle approximation sinθ≈θ, which fails badly at A=60∘.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2023 Jan Shift 1 & 2025 April Shift 1.

Direct-Vision vs Achromatic Prism Angle Equations [Critical Pitfall]

❌ Wrong Thinking (-1):

Confusing "Dispersion without deviation" with "Deviation without dispersion".

✓ Question-Proof Rule (+4):

Dispersion without deviation (Direct-vision): net mean deviation is zero: (μy​−1)A+(μy′​−1)A′=0. Achromatic: net dispersion is zero: (μv​−μr​)A+(μv′​−μr′​)A′=0.

Why: Targeting zero deviation requires canceling yellow/mean rays; targeting zero dispersion requires canceling violet-red ray separation.

PYQ Connection: JEE Main 2026 Jan 27 Shift 2: Specifically asked Direct-Vision Spectroscope angle A′.

Section 5: High-Yield Ray Optics Graphs & Critical Coordinates Analytical Geometry

u−v Hyperbolic Curve for Convex Lens

Axes: x-axis: Object distance u (Cartesian, u<0 for real object); y-axis: Image distance v (v>0 for real image)

v1​−u1​=f1​⟹v=u+fuf​
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • At u=−2f: v=+2f (Symmetric point where ∣u∣=∣v∣, magnification m=−1).
  • At u=−f: v→+∞ (Parallel emerging rays, principal focus).
  • At u→−∞: v→+f (Rays focus at second focal point F2​).
  • For −f<u<0 (Between optical center and focus): v<0 (Virtual erect magnified image, m>+1).
  • At optical center u→0−: v→0− (m→+1).

Asymptotes: Vertical asymptote at u=−f; Horizontal asymptote at v=+f.

What NTA Asks: Identifying the quadrant; extracting f from the intersection of curve with the line v=−u (which occurs exactly at (−2f,+2f)); and minimum physical separation between real object and real image: Dmin​=4f.

Physical Takeaway: The curve lies in the second quadrant (u<0,v>0) for real-to-real imaging and in the third quadrant (u<0,v<0) for real object with virtual image.

1/v vs 1/u Linear Plot for Thin Lens

Axes: x-axis: 1/u; y-axis: 1/v

v1​=(+1)⋅u1​+f1​⟹y=mx+c with Slope m=+1
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • Slope m=tanθ=+1 (Angle with positive x-axis is strictly 45∘ for ANY lens, converging or diverging).
  • y-intercept (1/u=0, i.e. u→∞): y0​=+f1​.
  • x-intercept (1/v=0, i.e. v→∞): x0​=−f1​.

Asymptotes: No asymptotes; this is a strictly linear transformation of the Gaussian equation spanning the entire paraxial domain.

What NTA Asks: Determining focal length from intercepts: f=y-intercept1​=−x-intercept1​. NTA frequently asks for the value or sign of the slope (+1).

Physical Takeaway: A positive slope of +1 is the mathematical signature of a thin lens, distinguishing it from a spherical mirror whose slope is −1.

u−v Hyperbolic Curve for Concave Mirror

Axes: x-axis: Object distance u (Cartesian, u<0 for real object); y-axis: Image distance v (v<0 for real image, v>0 for virtual image)

v1​+u1​=f1​⟹v=u−fuf​(with f=−∣f∣)
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • At u=−2∣f∣ (Center of Curvature C): v=−2∣f∣, magnification m=−1 (image coincides with object).
  • At u=−∣f∣ (Principal Focus F): v→±∞ (vertical asymptote).
  • At u→−∞: v→−∣f∣ (horizontal asymptote, image at focus).
  • For −∣f∣<u<0 (Between pole and focus): v>0 (virtual erect magnified image behind mirror, m>+1).
  • At pole u=0: v=0,m=+1.

Asymptotes: Vertical asymptote at u=−∣f∣=f; Horizontal asymptote at v=−∣f∣=f.

What NTA Asks: Extracting f from the intersection of the curve with the line v=u in the 3rd quadrant (occurs at (−2∣f∣,−2∣f∣)). Recognizing that both u and v are negative for a real image formed by a concave mirror.

Physical Takeaway: For real object and real image, the curve lies entirely in the 3rd quadrant (u<0,v<0). When object is inside focus, curve transitions to 2nd quadrant (u<0,v>0).

1/v vs 1/u Linear Plot for Spherical Mirror

Axes: x-axis: 1/u; y-axis: 1/v

v1​=(−1)⋅u1​+f1​⟹y=mx+c with Slope m=−1
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • Slope m=tanθ=−1 (Angle with positive x-axis is strictly 135∘ for ANY spherical mirror).
  • y-intercept (1/u=0, i.e. u→∞): y0​=+f1​.
  • x-intercept (1/v=0, i.e. v→∞): x0​=+f1​.
  • For Concave Mirror (f<0): both intercepts are negative, line passes through 3rd and 4th quadrants.
  • For Convex Mirror (f>0): both intercepts are positive, line passes through 1st and 2nd quadrants.

Asymptotes: No asymptotes; perfectly straight line with slope −1.

What NTA Asks: Slope comparison between lens (+1) and mirror (−1). Determining focal length from intercepts: f=y-intercept1​=x-intercept1​.

Physical Takeaway: The negative slope −1 directly reflects the plus sign in the mirror formula v1​+u1​=f1​.

Transverse Magnification m vs Object Distance u for Spherical Mirror

Axes: x-axis: Object distance u (Cartesian); y-axis: Magnification m

m=f−uf​(Concave: f=−∣f∣;Convex: f=+∣f∣)
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • For Concave Mirror (f=−∣f∣): m=−∣f∣−u−∣f∣​=∣f∣+u∣f∣​. At u=−∣f∣, vertical asymptote (m→±∞). At u=−2∣f∣, m=−1.
  • For Convex Mirror (f=+∣f∣): with real object (u<0), m=∣f∣+∣u∣∣f∣​. As u goes from 0 to −∞, m decreases monotonically from +1 to 0. Magnification is STRICTLY 0<m<1 (always virtual, erect, diminished).
  • At pole (u=0): m=+1 for both concave and convex mirrors.

Asymptotes: For concave mirror: vertical asymptote at u=f=−∣f∣. Horizontal asymptote at m=0 as u→−∞.

What NTA Asks: Differentiating concave from convex mirror from magnification behavior: real object with ∣m∣>1 or m<0 is GUARANTEED to be a concave mirror.

Physical Takeaway: Convex mirror can NEVER produce m<0 or m>1 for any real object position.

Deviation δ vs Angle of Incidence i for Prism

Axes: x-axis: Angle of incidence i (0∘ to 90∘); y-axis: Deviation angle δ

δ=i+e−Awith unique minimum at i=e=2A+δm​​
Key Critical Coordinates:
  • Single unique minimum at δ=δm​ (Condition of minimum deviation: ray passes symmetrically).
  • Asymmetric U-shape: the right wing (i>imin​) rises much more gradually than the left wing (i<imin​).
  • For any deviation δ>δm​, there are exactly TWO angles of incidence (i1​ and i2​=e1​) giving the same deviation (Principle of Optical Reversibility).
  • At minimum deviation: i1​=i2​=e=2A+δm​​ and internal angles r1​=r2​=2A​.

Asymptotes: No vertical asymptotes; curve is bounded between grazing incidence (i=90∘) and grazing emergence (e=90∘).

What NTA Asks: NTA asks for angle of emergence given one angle of incidence at deviation δ: i1​+i2​=A+δ. Also tests why the curve is asymmetric.

Physical Takeaway: At δm​, the two incident angles collapse into one: i=e.
